question: Should OpenClaw adopt earliest-layer path ownership, startup immutability, and the proposed closed monotonic exception set as the permanent opt-in managed-configuration contract?
rationale: Tests and lifecycle proof can validate this implementation, but they cannot decide whether this authority model is the product and security boundary OpenClaw wants to support long term.

options.title: Accept narrowed V1
options.body: Approve the opt-in startup-only contract as written, require the linked implementation to preserve no-flag behavior, and track writable layers or additional monotonic fields as separate RFC work.

options.title: Revise authority semantics
options.body: Keep the RFC in draft while maintainers change precedence, mutation, diagnostics, or monotonic exception rules before accepting a permanent contract.

options.title: Defer core support
options.body: Leave Lobster's overlay composition outside OpenClaw until a broader managed-configuration direction is sponsored.

recommendation.title: Accept narrowed V1
recommendation.body: Approve the opt-in startup-only contract as written, require the linked implementation to preserve no-flag behavior, and track writable layers or additional monotonic fields as separate RFC work.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest visible recent ownership across configuration behavior and security-sensitive config mutation paths.
